svg.title: YouLearn — lifecycle of a malicious upload, and where it is logged
svg.text: Lifecycle of a malicious upload
YouLearn in production — one OCI VM, docker compose, pull-based deploy. What each hop does with an infected file, and where that lands in the log store.
browser
instructor
proxy
Caddy · TLS
web
Next.js SSR
api
PHP 8.3
clamav
clamd :3310
mysql
sessions
logs
VictoriaLogs
THE REQUEST, STEP BY STEP
WHAT IT LOGS — ALL OF IT SEARCHABLE BY DATE
Instructor picks scanner-test.jpg and starts the upload
browser
POST /api/uploads declares kind, filename and size_bytes. The size is checked against
the ceiling (8 MiB image / 4 GiB video) before a single byte is accepted.
client only — nothing reaches a server log yet
Caddy terminates TLS and re-resolves the web upstream
proxy
dynamic a → web:3000, refresh 10s. It sets X-Forwarded-For, which is what makes the
caller’s real address available downstream at all.
JSON access log per request — status, path, duration, caller
IP. The `log` directive had to be added; Caddy writes none
by default.
The Next.js route authorises and attaches the bearer server-side
web
web/src/app/api/uploads/route.ts checks the session and the admin/enseignant role. The
access token never reaches client JavaScript.
thin · Next logs to stdout on a throw; a plain 403 here
leaves no line at all.
UploadController::begin opens a session row
api
A row in upload_sessions (user, kind, original_name, declared_size, 24 h TTL) plus an
empty .part file under /var/www/storage/tmp.
durable · the MySQL row is the real trace of this step — it
survives a redeploy, unlike any container log.
Chunks stream to disk — PATCH /uploads/{id}?offset=
api
5 MiB at a time, streamed straight to the .part file. An offset that disagrees with
received_bytes is a 409, never a silent append.
received_bytes is updated per chunk in MySQL; stdout stays
silent.
complete → FileStore::finalise sniffs the real content type
api
finfo says image/jpeg, so the type check passes. This is the step a bare EICAR file
could never survive — text/plain is refused here, before clamd is ever consulted.
nothing written — a refusal on type is a 422 like any other.
VirusScanner::assertClean hands clamd a path, not bytes
api → clamav
zSCAN /var/www/storage/tmp/{id}.part over TCP 3310. A path rather than INSTREAM, because
INSTREAM is capped by StreamMaxLength (25 MB) and a lecture may be four gigabytes.
On failure, api stdout: "[youlearn] scan_unavailable
reason=… host=clamav:3310". A scan that completes stays
quiet.
clamd matches the signature over the shared read-only volume
clamav
storage-data is mounted at the identical path in both containers, so the path means the
same thing on each side. YouLearn.SelfTest.Marker matches.
clamd stdout: "…/tmp/{id}.part: YouLearn.SelfTest.Marker
FOUND". LogClean is false, so a clean scan stays silent —
absence of a line is not evidence.
The bytes are deleted, then the request is refused 422
api
discardTemp() unlinks the .part file first — there is never a window in which an
infected file exists under a servable path. The signature name is withheld from the
response so it cannot be used as a tuning oracle.
api stdout: "[youlearn] malware_rejected signature=…
size_bytes=… path=…". The path ends in the upload id, which
joins to upload_sessions and therefore to the account.
The upload UI shows "Malware scan failed."
web → browser
cover-upload.tsx / video-upload.tsx switch on errorCode === "infected_file". The
scan-stripes state is what the user watched while steps 7–8 ran.
client only
Where you read it — vmui, over an SSH tunnel
Vector reads every container’s stdout and ships it to VictoriaLogs, which keeps 90 days on its own volume. vmui has no login, so it binds to 127.0.0.1 and the way in is the tunnel:
ssh -L 9428:127.0.0.1:9428 ubuntu@<instance> then open http://127.0.0.1:9428/select/vmui
_time:[2026-07-01, 2026-08-01] malware_rejected every refusal in July
_time:30d malware_rejected | stats count() how often it happens
`docker compose logs --since … --until …` still works and needs no tunnel, but it only sees what is still on the host: three 10 MB files per container, thrown away
every time the update timer recreates one. That is the reason the durable copy exists — not because grep is slow, but because the lines are gone.
THE TWO TIERS — ONE SHIPPED, ONE STILL TO BUILD
Tier 1 — record the event · NEXT
app-owned · permanent · already the house pattern
A security_events table
Mirror export_audit, which already stores actor, role, outcome,
reason, packed IP and user agent. ExportAuditRepository copies
almost verbatim.
Written from the scan path
outcome ∈ infected | scanner_unavailable | scan_timeout, plus
signature, sha256, byte size, declared filename, user_id, ip,
created_at.
A date-ranged admin page
/dashboard/security?from=&to= — an ordinary SSR page over an
indexed created_at, in the dashboard people already use. No SSH
client required.
What it adds over a log line
The identity. A log says which upload id was refused; the row says
which account, and turns "who keeps tripping the scanner" into a
GROUP BY.
Tier 2 — ship the container logs · SHIPPED
logs + logs-collector in docker-compose.prod.yml
VictoriaLogs v1.52 — the store
One Go binary, one volume, LogsQL, and vmui at /select/vmui.
Retention is LOGS_RETENTION, 90 days by default; the box is a 50
GB disk.
Vector 0.57 — the collector
Reads the docker socket, forwards over the Elasticsearch bulk
protocol. No plugin to keep current, and the socket goes to
nothing else.
Why not Loki, Dozzle, ELK
Loki + Grafana is the same idea one container heavier — take it if
you want alerting. Dozzle tails but keeps no history. ELK/Graylog
do not fit this VM.
Pinned and mirrored
Both images are copied into OCIR by the mirror workflow: Docker
Hub times out from af-casablanca-1 often enough to break a deploy.

One caveat worth keeping in view: a scan that finds nothing writes nothing. Absence of a line means the upload was clean OR the scanner was never asked — CLAMAV_ENABLED=false looks identical from here.
